cohort: Pregnant women with PCOS in the United States between 2004-2014, identified from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project Nationwide Inpatient Sample (HCUP-NIS) database
finding: Despite increases in demographic risk factors for pregnancy complications, the study found that rates of gestational diabetes, preterm premature rupture of membranes, preterm delivery, cesarean section, and wound complications decreased in women with PCOS between 2004-2014, while spontaneous vaginal delivery rates increased; however, congenital anomalies also increased.
mod_finding: Rates of cesarean section decreased from 57.3% in 2004 to 45.7% in 2014 (P < 0.001), while rates of spontaneous vaginal delivery increased from 37.4% in 2004 to 50.1% in 2014 (P < 0.001).
